title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
abstract: arXiv:2611.08438v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. Yet we continue to build increasingly powerful systems without fully understanding how they work, how they will behave in unfamiliar situations, or how to reliably control them. Mechanistic interpretability offers a path towards understanding these systems by studying their internal representations and computations, with the aim of evaluating, predicting, and controlling behaviour. We survey mechanistic interpretability for AI safety in order to answer the question: Does understanding how models work actually make them safer? We place mechanistic interpretability in the broader context of interpretability research and compare its mechanistic evidence with behavioural evaluation. We int

translated_title: 从内部理解人工智能：面向AI安全的机制可解释性研究现状
translated_abstract: 神经网络很可能是人类历史上最重要的人造物之一。随着这些系统变得更加强大和自主，它们造成社会危害的潜力也在增长，这使得AI安全成为我们这个时代的决定性挑战之一。然而，我们在尚未完全理解这些系统如何工作、它们在陌生情境中会如何表现、以及如何可靠地控制它们的情况下，仍在继续构建越来越强大的系统。机制可解释性通过研究这些系统的内部表示和计算，为理解这些系统提供了一条路径，其目标是评估、预测和控制模型行为。我们对面向AI安全的机制可解释性进行了综述，以回答这样一个问题：理解模型的工作原理真的能让它们更安全吗？我们将机制可解释性置于更广泛的可解释性研究背景之中，并将其机制性证据与行为评估进行了比较……
tldr: 本论文系统综述了机制可解释性在AI安全领域的研究现状，探讨通过理解模型内部表示与计算来评估、预测和控制AI行为，能否真正使AI系统更加安全。
en_tdlr: This paper surveys the state of mechanistic interpretability for AI safety, examining whether understanding models' internal representations and computations can actually make AI systems safer through evaluating, predicting, and controlling their behavior.
